\displaystyle=2\;\Box\kern-1.1pt\Box\;\Box\kern-1.1pt\Box+2\;\Box\kern-1.1pt\Box\kern-1.1pt\Box+\Box\kern-1.1pt\Box

Remark 3.29

(Section coefficients)
.

We can write

\displaystyle\langle\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\otimes\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$},\Delta_{{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$})\rangle

\displaystyle=\#\{A,A^{\prime}\subset\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}_{j}\;|A\cup A^{\prime}=\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$},\;\exists!\,\mathcal{I}\in\mathbf{IP}(A),\exists!\,\mathcal{I}^{\prime}\in\mathbf{IP}(A^{\prime}),

\displaystyle\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I})=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I}^{\prime})=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$},\mathcal{I}\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\mathcal{I}^{\prime}=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\}.

3.2.2
Bialgebras on interval partitions

We now show that the algebraic operations are compatible. The unit and the counit maps are given by

\displaystyle u\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}\mathbb{Q}\to\mathcal{H}_{\tiny\textbf{int}}

\displaystyle u\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}1\mapsto\mathsf{e}

\displaystyle\varepsilon\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}\mathcal{H}_{\tiny\textbf{int}}\to\mathbb{Q}

\displaystyle\varepsilon(x)=\begin{cases}x\;\text{if}\;x\in\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{StIP}_{0}]\\
0\;\text{else}\end{cases}

Theorem 3.30

(Bialgebras on interval partitions)
.

The following holds:

–

(\mathcal{H}_{\tiny\textbf{int}},\bullet,\Delta_{{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}},u,\varepsilon)
, is a bialgebra.

–

(\mathcal{H}_{\tiny\textbf{int}},{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}},\Delta_{\bullet},u,\varepsilon)
, is a connected filtered Hopf algebra, according to both
Equation

3
and
Equation

4
.

Lemma 3.31
.

Let
A,B\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 1},\;|A|,|B|<\infty
,
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}\in\mathbf{StIP}
, and
\mathcal{I}\in\mathbf{IP}(A),\mathcal{I}^{\prime}\in\mathbf{IP}(B)
. Assume

\displaystyle\mathcal{I}\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\mathcal{I}^{\prime}

\displaystyle=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}.

Recall that

\displaystyle\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}_{1},...,\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}_{m},\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime}_{1},...,\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime}_{n}\}

where for
i=1,...,n
,
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime}_{i}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=|\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}|+\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}_{i}
.
Then

1.

\displaystyle\mathcal{I}

\displaystyle=\mathcal{I}(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$})\uplus\mathcal{I}(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime}_{j}),

\displaystyle\mathcal{I}^{\prime}

\displaystyle=\mathcal{I}^{\prime}(B\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$})\uplus\mathcal{I}^{\prime}(B\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime}_{j}),

2.

\displaystyle\mathcal{I}(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$})\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\mathcal{I}^{\prime}(B\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}_{j})

\displaystyle=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},

\displaystyle\mathcal{I}(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime}_{j})\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\mathcal{I}^{\prime}(B\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime}_{j})

\displaystyle=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime}.

3.

\displaystyle\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I})

\displaystyle=\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I}(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}))\bullet\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I}(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime})),

\displaystyle\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I}^{\prime})

\displaystyle=\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I}^{\prime}(B\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}))\bullet\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I}^{\prime}(B\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime})).

Proof.

First, we have

\displaystyle\mathcal{I}

\displaystyle=\mathcal{I}(A)=\mathcal{I}(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\uplus A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime}_{j})

\displaystyle=\{\mathcal{I}_{j}\cap c|j\in J,c\in\mathbf{cliques}(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\uplus A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime}_{j})\}\setminus\{\emptyset\}

\displaystyle=\{\mathcal{I}_{j}\cap c|j\in J,c\in\mathbf{cliques}(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$})\uplus\mathbf{cliques}(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime}_{j})\}\setminus\{\emptyset\}

\displaystyle=\{\mathcal{I}_{j}\cap c|j\in J,c\in\mathbf{cliques}(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$})\}\setminus\{\emptyset\}

\displaystyle\uplus\{\mathcal{I}_{j}\cap c|j\in J,c\in\mathbf{cliques}(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime})\}\setminus\{\emptyset\}

\displaystyle=\mathcal{I}(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$})\uplus\mathcal{I}(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime}_{j}).

Analogously one shows that
\mathcal{I}^{\prime}=\mathcal{I}^{\prime}(B\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$})\uplus\mathcal{I}^{\prime}(B\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime}_{j})
.
Therefore

\displaystyle\mathcal{I}(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$})\uplus\mathcal{I}(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime})\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}(\mathcal{I}(B\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$})\uplus\mathcal{I}(B\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime})=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}.

which holds if and only if

\displaystyle\mathcal{I}(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$})\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\mathcal{I}^{\prime}(B\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$})=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},

and

\displaystyle\mathcal{I}(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime})\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\mathcal{I}^{\prime}(B\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime})=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime},

Finally, since we can write

\displaystyle\mathcal{I}

\displaystyle=\{I_{s,1},I_{s,m},I_{t^{\prime},1},...,I_{t^{\prime},n}\}

with

\displaystyle\mathcal{I}(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$})=\{I_{s,1},I_{s,m}\},

\displaystyle\mathcal{I}(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime})=\{I_{t^{\prime},1},...,I_{t^{\prime},n}\}

we have

\displaystyle\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I})

\displaystyle=\mathbf{std}(\{I_{s,1},...,I_{s,m}\})\uplus\left(|\bigcup_{j=1}^{m}I_{s,j}|+\mathbf{std}(\{I_{t,1},...,I_{t,n}\})\right)

\displaystyle\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I}(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}))\bullet\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I}(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime})).

And analogously one shows that
\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I}^{\prime}(B\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}))\bullet\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I}^{\prime}(B\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime}))

∎

Proof.

We show that
\Delta_{{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$})=\Delta_{{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$})\bullet\Delta_{{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$})
.
We have

\displaystyle\Delta_{{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$})

\displaystyle=\sum_{A\cup A^{\prime}=\bigcup\left(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}\right)}\;\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathcal{I}\in\mathbf{IP}(A),\mathcal{I}\in\mathbf{IP}(A^{\prime})\\
\\
\mathcal{I}\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\mathcal{I}^{\prime}=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}\end{subarray}}\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I})\otimes\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I}^{\prime}).

Thanks to
Lemma

3.31
, we can write

\displaystyle\Delta_{{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$})

\displaystyle=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$})\cup(A^{\prime}\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$})=\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\\
\\
(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime})\cup(A^{\prime}\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime})=\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime}\end{subarray}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathcal{I}\in\mathbf{IP}(A),\,\mathcal{I}^{\prime}\in\mathbf{IP}(A^{\prime})\\
\\
\mathcal{I}(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$})\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\mathcal{I}^{\prime}(A^{\prime}\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$})=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\\
\\
\mathcal{I}(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime})\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\mathcal{I}(A^{\prime}\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime})=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime}\end{subarray}}\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I}(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}))\bullet\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I}(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime}))

\displaystyle\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\quad\otimes\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I}^{\prime}(A^{\prime}\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$})\bullet\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I}^{\prime}(A^{\prime}\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime}))

\displaystyle=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}A_{1}\cup A_{1}^{\prime}=\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\\
\\
A_{2}\cup A_{2}^{\prime}=\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime}\end{subarray}}\;\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathcal{I}_{1}\in\mathbf{IP}(A_{1}),\mathcal{I}_{1}^{\prime}\in\mathbf{IP}(A_{1}^{\prime})\\
\\
\mathcal{I}_{2}\in\mathbf{IP}(A_{2}),\mathcal{I}_{2}^{\prime}\in\mathbf{IP}(A_{2}^{\prime})\\
\\
\mathcal{I}_{1}\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\mathcal{I}_{1}^{\prime}=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},\;\mathcal{I}_{2}\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\mathcal{I}_{2}^{\prime}=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime}\end{subarray}}\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I}_{1})\bullet\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I}_{2})\otimes\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I}_{1}^{\prime})\bullet\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I}_{2}^{\prime})

\displaystyle=\sum_{A_{1}\cup A_{1}^{\prime}=\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}}\;\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathcal{I}_{1}\in\mathbf{IP}(A_{1})\\
\mathcal{I}_{1}^{\prime}\in\mathbf{IP}(A_{1}^{\prime})\\
\mathcal{I}_{1}\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\mathcal{I}_{1}^{\prime}=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\end{subarray}}\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I}_{1})\otimes\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I}_{1}^{\prime})\bullet\sum_{A_{2}\cup A_{2}^{\prime}=\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime}}\;\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathcal{I}_{2}\in\mathbf{IP}(A_{2})\\
\mathcal{I}_{2}^{\prime}\in\mathbf{IP}(A_{2}^{\prime})\\
\mathcal{I}_{2}\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\mathcal{I}_{2}^{\prime}=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime}\end{subarray}}\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I}_{2})\otimes\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I}_{2}^{\prime})

Using
Lemma

3.26
, we have

\displaystyle\sum_{A_{2}\cup A_{2}^{\prime}=\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime}}\;\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathcal{I}_{2}\in\mathbf{IP}(A_{2}),\mathcal{I}_{2}^{\prime}\in\mathbf{IP}(A_{2}^{\prime})\\
\\
\mathcal{I}_{2}\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\mathcal{I}_{2}^{\prime}=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}^{\prime}\end{subarray}}\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I}_{2})\otimes\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I}_{2}^{\prime})

\displaystyle=\sum_{B\cup B^{\prime}=\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}}\;\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathcal{J}\in\mathbf{IP}(B),\mathcal{J}^{\prime}\in\mathbf{IP}(B^{\prime})\\
\\
\mathcal{J}\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\mathcal{J}^{\prime}=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}\end{subarray}}\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{J})\otimes\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{J}^{\prime}).

Therefore

\displaystyle\Delta_{{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$})

\displaystyle=\Delta_{{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$})\bullet\Delta_{{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$})

\displaystyle=\sum_{A\cup A^{\prime}=\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}}\;\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathcal{I}\in\mathbf{IP}(A),\mathcal{I}^{\prime}\in\mathbf{IP}(A^{\prime})\\
\\
\mathcal{I}\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\mathcal{I}^{\prime}=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\end{subarray}}\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I})\otimes\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I}^{\prime})

\displaystyle\qquad\bullet\sum_{B\cup B^{\prime}=\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}}\;\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathcal{J}\in\mathbf{IP}(B),\mathcal{J}^{\prime}\in\mathbf{IP}(B^{\prime})\\
\\
\mathcal{J}\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\mathcal{J}^{\prime}=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}\end{subarray}}\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{J})\otimes\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{J}^{\prime}).

Dually, it follows that

(\mathcal{H}_{\tiny\textbf{int}},{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}},\Delta_{\bullet},u,\varepsilon)

is also a bialgebra. We recall the well-known fact that any connected filtered bialgebra is automatically a Hopf algebra, see
[
11
]
[Corollary 5].
∎

The following remark is about how, under certain assumptions, one can learn about the structure of an algebra by endowing it with a Hopf algebra structure.

Remark 3.32

(Polynomial algebra)
.

We recall the well-known result that any filtered Hopf algebra is isomorphic, as an algebra, to a polynomial algebra. See
[
4
]
[Theorem 4.4.1]. Therefore,
(\mathcal{H}_{\tiny\textbf{int}},{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}})
is a free commutative algebra.

Remark 3.33
.

We provide another description of the Hopf algebra from
Theorem

3.30
, by showing that it is isomorphic to a Hopf algebra on words, where the letters are positive integers.
Let
V\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\mathbb{Q}[\mathbb{N}_{\geq 1}]
, then

\displaystyle\Phi\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb{N}}V^{\otimes n}\to(\mathcal{H}_{\tiny\textbf{int}},\bullet),

defined as the unique extension of

\displaystyle\Phi(n)\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\{\{1,2,...,n\}\}

to a map of associative algebras, is a linear isomorphism.
We denote with
♠
the concatenation of tensors. If we restrict
\Phi
to words on positive integers, which form a linear basis, we obtain an injection onto a basis for the codomain, the set
\mathbf{StIP}
. Indeed, we have:

\displaystyle\Phi(n_{1}\text{♠}n_{2}\text{♠}\;\cdots\text{♠}\;n_{k})

\displaystyle=\Phi(n_{1})\bullet\Phi(n_{2})\bullet\cdots\bullet\Phi(n_{k})

\displaystyle=\left\{\{1,2,...,n_{1}\},\{n_{1}+1,\dots,n_{1}+n_{2}\},\dots,\{\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}n_{j}+1,...,\sum_{j=1}^{k}n_{j}\}\right\}.

As an example

\displaystyle\Phi(1\text{♠}3\text{♠}2)=\left\{\{1\},\{2,3,4\},\{5,6\}\right\}.

We can use
\Phi
to define a product on words, which is just a relabeling of
♠
. We define on basis elements

\displaystyle m_{1}\;\text{♠}\;m_{2}\;\text{♠}\;\cdots\;\text{♠}\;m_{\ell}\;

\displaystyle\underset{\tiny\textup{wrd}}{{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}}\;n_{1}\;\text{♠}\;n_{2}\;\text{♠}\;\cdots\;\text{♠}\;n_{k}

\displaystyle\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\Phi^{-1}\left(\Phi(m_{1}\;\text{♠}\;m_{2}\;\text{♠}\;\cdots\;\text{♠}\;m_{\ell})\;{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}\;\Phi(n_{1}\;\text{♠}\;n_{2}\;\text{♠}\;\cdots\;\text{♠}\;n_{k})\right).

For example

\displaystyle 2\;\underset{\tiny\textup{wrd}}{{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}}\;2

\displaystyle\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\Phi^{-1}(\Phi(2)\;{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}\;\Phi(2))

\displaystyle=\Phi^{-1}(\ \Box\kern-1.1pt\Box\ {{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}\ \Box\kern-1.1pt\Box\ )

\displaystyle=\Phi^{-1}(\ {\color[rgb]{1,0,0}2}\ \Box\kern-1.1pt\Box\ \Box\kern-1.1pt\Box+{\color[rgb]{1,0,0}2}\ \Box\kern-1.1pt\Box\kern-1.1pt\Box+\Box\kern-1.1pt\Box\ )

\displaystyle={\color[rgb]{1,0,0}2}\,2\text{♠}2+{\color[rgb]{1,0,0}2}\,3+2,

\displaystyle 1\text{♠}2\;\underset{\tiny\textup{wrd}}{{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}}\;1\text{♠}1

\displaystyle={\color[rgb]{1,0,0}3}\,1\text{♠}2\text{♠}1+{\color[rgb]{1,0,0}3}\,1\text{♠}2+1\text{♠}2\text{♠}1\text{♠}1

\displaystyle+{\color[rgb]{1,0,0}6}\,1\text{♠}1\text{♠}2+{\color[rgb]{1,0,0}3}\,1\text{♠}1\text{♠}1\text{♠}2+{\color[rgb]{1,0,0}2}1\text{♠}1\text{♠}2\text{♠}1.

Then, in analogy to
Theorem

3.30

–

(\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb{N}}V^{\otimes n},\text{♠},\Delta_{\underset{\tiny\textup{wrd}}{{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}}})
is a bialgebra,

–

(\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb{N}}V^{\otimes n},\underset{\tiny\textup{wrd}}{{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}},\Delta_{\text{♠}})
is a connected filtered (by the length of the words, see
Equation

4
) Hopf algebra.

3.3
Signature of an interval partition

We define a family of linear maps on the dual of
\mathcal{H}_{\tiny\textbf{int}}
, indexed by
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\in\mathbf{StIP}
. These maps, encode “occurrences” of other standardized interval partitions in

\mathfrak{L}

.

Definition 3.34

(Signature of an interval partition)
.

For
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\in\mathbf{StIP}
, define the linear map

\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$})\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}\mathcal{H}_{\tiny\textbf{int}}\to\mathbb{Q}
via

\displaystyle\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}),\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\Big\rangle\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\#\{A\subset\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}|\;\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(A))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\},\quad\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\in\mathbf{StIP}.

Remark 3.35
.

The condition
\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(A))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}
tells us that we count

\mathfrak{s}

, each time we find a pattern that is equal to

\mathfrak{s}

or coarser. Let
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}=\{\{1\},\{2\},\{3,4\}\}
, and
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}=\{\{1\},\{2\}\}
.

\displaystyle\text{For}\;A=\{3,4\},\;\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(A))

\displaystyle=\{\{1,2\}\}\geq\{\{1\},\{2\}\}.

So that if we look for a fine pattern (arbitrary gaps) we also count coarse pattern (consecutive values), while if we look for a coarse pattern we discard arbitrary gaps and only keep consecutive values. Let
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}=\{\{1\},\{2\},\{3,4\}\}
, and
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}=\{\{1,2\},\{3\}\}
.

\displaystyle\text{For}\;A=\{2,3,4\},\;\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(A))

\displaystyle=\{\{1\},\{2,3\}\}\perp\{\{1,2\},\{3\}\},

i.e., the structure of the gaps needs to be respected.

Remark 3.36
.

When we count the occurrences of an interval partition,
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}=\mathbf{n}_{1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{k}
(conveniently written taking the product
\bullet
of single blocks partitions,
\mathbf{n}_{j}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\{[n_{j}]\},n_{j}\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 1}
) in a single block partition, i.e.
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}=\mathbf{N}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\{[N]\},N\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 1}
, we have

\displaystyle\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}),\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\Big\rangle=\binom{N-(n_{1}+...+n_{k})+k}{k}.

(5)

which are the weak
k+1
compositions of
N-(n_{1}+...+n_{k})
. For example, if we have
N=9,n_{1}=3,n_{2}=5
, the three possible constellations

correspond to
(1,0,0),(0,1,0),(0,0,1)
respectively: i.e. the weak
3
compositions of
1
.

3.3.1
Character property and Chen’s identity

We call these maps
signatures
for interval partitions, motivated by the following result.

Theorem 3.37

(Character property)
.

The maps
(\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}))_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}}
are characters under the product
♠
. Let
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\in\mathbf{StIP}_{N}
, with
N\in\mathbb{N}
. For all
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}\in\mathbf{StIP}
, we have

\displaystyle\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}),\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\Big\rangle\cdot\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}),\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}\Big\rangle=\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}),\,\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\;{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}\;\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}\Big\rangle.

(6)

Remark 3.38

(Single blocks)
.

Let
\mathbf{N}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\{[N]\}
,
\mathbf{m}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\{[m]\}
,
\mathbf{n}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\{[n]\}
. Then we have

\displaystyle\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\mathbf{N}),\mathbf{m}\Big\rangle\cdot\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\mathbf{N}),\mathbf{n}\Big\rangle

\displaystyle=(N-m+1)(N-n+1)

thanks to
Remark

3.36
. Since

\displaystyle\mathbf{m}\;{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}\;\mathbf{n}

\displaystyle=\mathbf{m}\bullet\mathbf{n}+\mathbf{n}\bullet\mathbf{m}+2\sum_{i=1}^{\min(m,n)-1}\{[m+n-i]\}

\displaystyle+(\max(m,n)-\min(m,n)+1)\{[\max(m,n)]\}

using again
Remark

3.36
, we obtain

\displaystyle\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\mathbf{N}),\,\mathbf{m}\;{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}\;\mathbf{n}\Big\rangle

\displaystyle=2\binom{N-(m+n)+2}{2}+2\sum_{i=1}^{\min(m,n)-1}(N-(m+n-i)+1)

\displaystyle+(\max(m,n)-\min(m,n)+1)(N-\max(m,n)+1)

It is easy to show that

\displaystyle\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\mathbf{N}),\mathbf{m}\Big\rangle\cdot\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\mathbf{N}),\mathbf{n}\Big\rangle

\displaystyle=\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\mathbf{N}),\,\mathbf{m}\;{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}\;\mathbf{n}\Big\rangle

We now state several lemmas needed for the proof of
Theorem

3.37
.

Lemma 3.39

(

\mathfrak{s}

-refinement of
\mathcal{I}
)
.

Let
\mathcal{I}\in\mathbf{IP}
and
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\in\mathbf{StIP}
. If

\displaystyle\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I})\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},

then there exists a unique refinement
\mathcal{I}_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}}
of
\mathcal{I}
such that

\displaystyle\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I}_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}})=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}.

Example 3.40
.

Let
\mathcal{I}=\{\{5\},\{6\},\{10,11,12\}\}
and
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}=\{\{1\},\{2\},\{3,4\},\{5\}\}
. Then:

\displaystyle\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I})\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}

and

\displaystyle\mathcal{I}_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}}=\{\{5\},\{6\},\{10,11\},\{12\}\}

Proof.

Let

\displaystyle\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I})\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}.

We recall the notation used in
Definition

3.7
. Let
i_{1},\dots,i_{\ell_{1}},\dots,i_{\ell_{2}},\dots,i_{\ell_{k}}\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 1}
such that

\displaystyle i_{1}\prec\cdots\prec i_{\ell_{1}}<i_{\ell_{1}+1}\prec\cdots\prec i_{\ell_{2}}<\cdots<i_{\ell_{k-1}+1}\prec\cdots\prec i_{\ell_{k}},

where
i\prec j\iff j-i=1
.
Then

\displaystyle\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I})\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\mathbf{std}(\{\{i_{1},\dots,i_{\ell_{1}}\},\{i_{\ell_{1}+1},\dots,i_{\ell_{2}}\},\dots,\{i_{\ell_{k-1}+1},\dots,i_{\ell_{k}}\}\})

\displaystyle\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\{\{1,\dots,\ell_{1}\},\{\ell_{1}+1,\dots,\ell_{2}\},\dots,\{\ell_{k-1}+1,\dots,\ell_{k}\}\}

\displaystyle\geq\{\{1{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}|},\dots,{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}|}\ell_{1}\},\{\ell_{1}+1{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}|},\dots,{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}|}\ell_{2}\},\dots,\{\ell_{k-1}+1{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}|},\dots,{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}|}\ell_{k}\}\}=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}.

where

\displaystyle 1\prec\cdots\prec\ell_{1}\prec\ell_{1}+1\prec\cdots\prec\ell_{2}<\cdots<\ell_{k-1}+1\prec\cdots\prec\ell_{k}

and the
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}|}
indicate potential “cuts”, which lead to a different
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\in\mathbf{StIP}
. Clearly only

\displaystyle\{\{i_{1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}|},\dots,{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}|}i_{\ell_{1}}\},\{i_{\ell_{1}+1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}|},\dots,{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}|}i_{\ell_{2}}\},\dots,\{i_{\ell_{k-1}+1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}|},\dots,{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}|}i_{\ell_{k}}\}\}

does the job.
∎

Lemma 3.41
.

Let
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$},\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\in\mathbf{StIP}
. Then the following holds

\displaystyle\Big\{A,B\subset\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\;|\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(A))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(B))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}\Big\}

\displaystyle\quad=\biguplus_{\begin{subarray}{c}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$},C)\in\mathbf{StIP}\times\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\\
\\
\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(C))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\end{subarray}}\Big\{A,B\subset\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\;|A\cup B=C,\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(A))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(B))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$},

\displaystyle\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(A)_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}}\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(B)_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}})=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\Big\}.

where the union is taken over disjoint sets (possibly empty).

Proof.

Let
(A,B)
be an element of the LHS. Then there exists a unique pair
(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$},C)
such that it belongs to one of the sets on the RHS. We have
C\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=A\cup B
and
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(A)_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}}\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(B)_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}}).
The inequality
\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(C))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}
holds since

\displaystyle\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(C))\geq\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(A)\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(B))\geq\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(A)_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}}\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(B)_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}})=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}.

From left to right: the first inequality is due to
Corollary

3.16
, while the second is due to
Lemma

3.15
.

The other inclusion is trivial.
∎

Lemma 3.42

(Zooming in)
.

Let
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$},\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\in\mathbf{StIP}
,
(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$},C)\in\mathbf{StIP}\times\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}
. Assume that
\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(C))=\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$}\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}
. Then

\displaystyle\#\left\{\left.A,A^{\prime}\subset\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\;\right|A\cup A^{\prime}=C,\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(A))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(A^{\prime}))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$},\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(A)_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}}\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(A^{\prime})_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}})=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\right\}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\#\left\{\left.A,A^{\prime}\subset\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$}\;\right|A\cup A^{\prime}=\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$},\;\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$}(A))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$}(A^{\prime}))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$},\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$}(A)_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}}\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$}(A^{\prime})_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}}=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\right\}.

Proof.

Immediate.
∎

Lemma 3.43

(Invariance)
.

Let
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$},\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$}\in\mathbf{StIP}
such that
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$}\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}
. Then

\displaystyle\Big\{A,A^{\prime}\subset\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$}\;|A\cup A^{\prime}=\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$},\;\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$}(A))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$}(A^{\prime}))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$},\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$}(A)_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}}\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$}(A^{\prime})_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}}=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\Big\}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\{A,A^{\prime}\subset\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\;|A\cup A^{\prime}=\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$},\;\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A^{\prime}))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$},\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A)_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}}\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A^{\prime})_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}}=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\}.

Proof.

Denote the set on the left-hand side with
\textup{Set}_{0}

and the one on the right-hand side with
\textup{Set}_{1}
.
Let
(A,A^{\prime})\in\textup{Set}_{1}
. Since
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$}\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}
means that
\forall i\in I\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}\exists j\in J\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}_{i}\subset\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$}_{j}
and since

\displaystyle\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$}(A)\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\{c\cap\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$}_{j}|c\in\mathbf{cliques}(A),j\in J\}\setminus\{\emptyset\}

\displaystyle\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A)\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\{c\cap\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}_{j}|c\in\mathbf{cliques}(A),j\in J\}\setminus\{\emptyset\}

we have
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$}(A)\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A)
and, analogously,
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$}(A^{\prime})\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A^{\prime})
. This means that
\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$}(A))\geq\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}
and
\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$}(A^{\prime}))\geq\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A^{\prime}))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}
. Therefore
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$}(A)
and
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$}(A^{\prime})
can be refined so that
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$}(A)_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}}\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$}(A^{\prime})_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}}=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A)_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}}\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A^{\prime})_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}}=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}
, see
Lemma

3.39
. So,
(A,A^{\prime})\in\textup{Set}_{0}
. For the other direction, let
(A,A^{\prime})\in\textup{Set}_{0}
. Since
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$}(A)_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}}\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$}(A^{\prime})_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}}=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}
, using
Lemma

3.17
, we have

\displaystyle\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A)\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$}(A)_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}}

\displaystyle\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A^{\prime})\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{h}$}(A^{\prime})_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}}.

Then it is immediate to verify that
(A,A^{\prime})\in\textup{Set}_{1}
.
∎

Lemma 3.44

(Recovering section coefficients)
.

Let
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$},\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\in\mathbf{StIP}
. Then:

\displaystyle\left\{A,A^{\prime}\subset\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\;\Big|A\cup A^{\prime}=\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$},\;\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A^{\prime}))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$},\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A)_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}}\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A^{\prime})_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}}=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\right\}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\left\{A,A^{\prime}\subset\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\;\Big|A\cup A^{\prime}=\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$},\;\exists!\,\mathcal{I}\in\mathbf{IP}(A),\exists!\,\mathcal{I}^{\prime}\in\mathbf{IP}(A^{\prime}),\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I})=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I}^{\prime})=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$},\mathcal{I}\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\mathcal{I}^{\prime}=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\right\}.

In particular, see
Remark

3.29

\displaystyle\#\{A,A^{\prime}\subset\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\;|A\cup A^{\prime}=\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$},\;\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A^{\prime}))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$},\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A)_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}}\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A^{\prime})_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}}=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\}

\displaystyle=\langle\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\otimes\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$},\Delta_{{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$})\rangle.

Proof.

Denote the set on the left-hand side with
\textup{Set}_{0}

and the one on the right-hand side with
\textup{Set}_{1}
.
Let
(A,A^{\prime})\in\text{Set}_{0}
, then
A\cup A^{\prime}=\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}
,
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A)_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}}\in\mathbf{IP}(A)
and
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A^{\prime})_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}}\in\mathbf{IP}(A^{\prime})
,
\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A)_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}})=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}
,
\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A^{\prime})_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}})=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}
,
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A)_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}}\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A^{\prime})_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}}=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}
. Let
(A,A^{\prime})\in\text{Set}_{1}
, then
A\cup A^{\prime}=\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}
. Since
\mathcal{I}\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\mathcal{I}^{\prime}=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}
, with
\mathcal{I}\in\mathbf{IP}(A)
and
\mathcal{I}^{\prime}\in\mathbf{IP}(A^{\prime})
, we have
\mathcal{I}\leq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A)
,
\mathcal{I}^{\prime}\leq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A^{\prime})
, and
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}=\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I})\leq\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A))
,
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}=\mathbf{std}(\mathcal{I}^{\prime})\leq\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A^{\prime}))
as well. Therefore, using
Lemma

3.39
, we have
\mathcal{I}=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A)_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}}
and
\mathcal{I}^{\prime}=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}(A)_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}}
.

∎

Proof of
Theorem

3.37
.

\displaystyle\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}),\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\Big\rangle\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}),\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}\Big\rangle

\displaystyle=|\{A,B\subset\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\;|\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(A))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(B))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}\}|

\displaystyle=|\biguplus_{\begin{subarray}{c}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$},C)\in\mathbf{StIP}\times\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\\
\\
\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(C))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\end{subarray}}\{A,B\subset\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\;|A\cup B=C,\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(A))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(B))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$},

\displaystyle\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(A)_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}}\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(B)_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}})=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\}|

\displaystyle=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$},C)\in\mathbf{StIP}\times\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\\
\\
\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(C))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\end{subarray}}\langle{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\otimes\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}),\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\rangle=\sum_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\in\mathbf{StIP}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}C\in\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\\
\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(C))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\end{subarray}}\langle{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\otimes\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}),\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\rangle

\displaystyle=\sum_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\in\mathbf{StIP}}\langle{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\otimes\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}),\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\rangle\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}C\in\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\\
\mathbf{std}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(C))\geq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\end{subarray}}1=\sum_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\in\mathbf{StIP}}\langle{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\otimes\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}),\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\rangle\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}),\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\Big\rangle

\displaystyle=\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}),\sum_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\in\mathbf{StIP}}\langle{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\otimes\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}),\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\rangle\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\Big\rangle=\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}),\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\,{{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}\,\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}\Big\rangle.

We used
Lemma

3.41
for the second equality and
Lemmas

3.42
,
3.43
and
3.44
for the third one.
∎

Example 3.45
.

In the following expression, we write

Since
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}=\Box\kern-1.1pt\Box\kern-1.1pt\Box\kern-1.1pt\Box

,
\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}),\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}\Big\rangle=3

we obtain

\displaystyle\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}),\Box\;\Box\kern-1.1pt\Box\Big\rangle=\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}),\Box\kern-1.1pt\Box\;\Box\Big\rangle=3,

\displaystyle\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}),\Box\;\Box\kern-1.1pt\Box\;\Box\Big\rangle=\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}),\Box\kern-1.1pt\Box\;\Box\;\Box\Big\rangle=\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}),\Box\;\Box\;\Box\kern-1.1pt\Box\Big\rangle=1,

and computing

\displaystyle\Box\kern-1.1pt\Box\ {{\text{\color[rgb]{1,0.47,0.62}{♠}}}}\ \Box\;\Box

\displaystyle+\Box\;\Box\kern-1.1pt\Box\;\Box+\Box\kern-1.1pt\Box\;\Box\;\Box,

we have

\displaystyle\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}),\Box\kern-1.1pt\Box\Big\rangle\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}),\Box\;\Box\Big\rangle

\displaystyle=\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}),\Box\kern-1.1pt\Box\Big\rangle+2\;\;\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}),\Box\kern-1.1pt\Box\;\Box\Big\rangle+2\;\;\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}),\Box\;\Box\kern-1.1pt\Box\Big\rangle

.

We also have a form of Chen’s identity.

Theorem 3.46

(Chen’s identity)
.

The maps
(\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}))_{\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}}
satisfy a form of Chen’s identity, i.e., for all
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$},\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}\in\mathbf{StIP}
:

\displaystyle\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}),\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\Big\rangle=\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$})\otimes\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}),\Delta_{\bullet}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$})\Big\rangle

(7)

Remark 3.47
.

As a consequence of Chen’s identity, we can sum over numbers of the form of
Equation

5
to calculate explicitly any occurrence. Let
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}=\mathbf{N}_{1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{N}_{m}
and
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}=\mathbf{n}_{1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{k}
, where
m,k\in\mathbb{N}
and
\forall i\in[m],\forall j\in[k],N_{i}\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 1},n_{j}\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 1},\mathbf{N}_{i}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\{[N_{i}]\},\mathbf{n}_{j}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\{[n_{j}]\}
. Then

\displaystyle\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}),\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\Big\rangle=\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\mathbf{N}_{1})\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathsf{IPC}(\mathbf{N}_{m}),\Delta_{\bullet}^{m}(\mathbf{n}_{1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{k})\Big\rangle

\displaystyle=\sum_{0\leq i_{1}\leq\cdots\leq i_{m-1}\leq k}\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\mathbf{N}_{1}),\mathbf{n}_{1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{i_{1}}\Big\rangle\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\mathbf{N}_{2}),\mathbf{n}_{i_{1}+1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{i_{2}}\Big\rangle\cdots

\displaystyle\qquad\cdots\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\mathbf{N}_{m}),\mathbf{n}_{i_{m-1}+1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{k}\Big\rangle

\displaystyle=\sum_{0\leq i_{1}\leq\cdots\leq i_{m-1}\leq k}\Biggl(\mkern-1.0mu\begin{matrix}N_{1}-\sum\limits_{j=1}^{i_{1}}n_{j}+i_{1}\\
i_{1}\end{matrix}\mkern-1.0mu\Biggr.\kern-3.0pt\Biggl.\vphantom{\begin{matrix}N_{1}-\sum\limits_{j=1}^{i_{1}}n_{j}+i_{1}\\
i_{1}\end{matrix}}\mkern-1.0mu\Biggr)\Biggl(\mkern-1.0mu\begin{matrix}N_{2}-\sum\limits_{j=i_{1}+1}^{i_{2}}n_{j}+i_{2}-i_{1}\\
i_{2}-i_{1}\end{matrix}\mkern-1.0mu\Biggr.\kern-3.0pt\Biggl.\vphantom{\begin{matrix}N_{2}-\sum\limits_{j=i_{1}+1}^{i_{2}}n_{j}+i_{2}-i_{1}\\
i_{2}-i_{1}\end{matrix}}\mkern-1.0mu\Biggr)\cdots

\displaystyle\qquad\cdots\Biggl(\mkern-1.0mu\begin{matrix}N_{m}-\sum\limits_{j=i_{m-1}+1}^{k}n_{j}+k-i_{m-1}\\
k-i_{m-1}\end{matrix}\mkern-1.0mu\Biggr.\kern-3.0pt\Biggl.\vphantom{\begin{matrix}N_{m}-\sum\limits_{j=i_{m-1}+1}^{k}n_{j}+k-i_{m-1}\\
k-i_{m-1}\end{matrix}}\mkern-1.0mu\Biggr)

To prove
Theorem

3.46
, we need three lemmas.

Lemma 3.48
.

Let
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}\in\mathbf{StIP}

\mathfrak{t}

\displaystyle\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\{[n_{1}]\}\bullet\{[n_{2}]\}\bullet\cdots\bullet\{[n_{k}]\}

\displaystyle=\left\{\{1,\dots,n_{1}\},\{n_{1}+1,\dots,n_{1}+n_{2}\},\dots,\{\sum_{i=1}^{k-1}n_{i}+1,\dots,\sum_{i=1}^{k}n_{i}\}\right\}.

where
n_{1},\dots,n_{k}\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 1}
and
k\in\mathbb{N}
.
Let
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\in\mathbf{StIP}
such that
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}\leq\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}
. Then

\mathfrak{s}

can be written as

\mathfrak{s}

\displaystyle\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\{[\sum_{i=1}^{j_{1}}n_{i}]\}\bullet\{[\sum_{i=j_{1}+1}^{j_{2}}n_{i}]\}\bullet\cdots\bullet\{[\sum_{i=j_{N-1}+1}^{j_{N}}n_{i}]\}

\displaystyle=\{\{1,\dots,\sum_{i=1}^{j_{1}}n_{i}\},\{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{1}}n_{i}+1,\dots,\sum_{i=1}^{j_{2}}n_{i}\},\dots,\{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{N-1}}n_{i}+1,\dots,\sum_{i=1}^{j_{N}}n_{i}\}\}.

where

\displaystyle j_{1},\dots,j_{N}\in\mathbb{N},1\leq j_{1}<\dots<j_{N}=k,1\leq N\leq k.

In particular, for
t\in\{0\}\cup{N}
, setting
j_{t}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=0
, we have

\displaystyle\{[n_{1}]\}\bullet\cdots\bullet\{[n_{j_{t}}]\}

\displaystyle\leq\{[\sum_{i=1}^{j_{1}}n_{i}]\}\bullet\cdots\bullet\{[\sum_{i=j_{t-1}+1}^{j_{t}}n_{i}]\},

and

\displaystyle\{[n_{j_{t}+1}]\}\bullet\cdots\bullet\{[n_{j_{N}}]\}

\displaystyle\leq\{[\sum_{i=j_{t}+1}^{j_{t+1}}n_{i}]\}\bullet\cdots\bullet\{[\sum_{i=j_{N-1}+1}^{j_{N}}n_{i}]\},

where
\{[n_{1}]\}\bullet\cdots\bullet\{[n_{0}]\}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\mathsf{e}
and

\{[n_{j_{N+1}}]\}\bullet\cdots\bullet\{[n_{j_{N}}]\}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\mathsf{e}
.

Proof.

The fact that

\mathfrak{s}

is of the given form is simply an explicit description of the interval partitions which are coarser than

\mathfrak{t}

.
∎

Lemma 3.49
.

Let
\mathbf{n}_{1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{k}\in\mathbf{StIP}
, where
k\in\mathbb{N}
and
\forall r\in[k]\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}n_{r}\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 1},\mathbf{n}_{i}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\{[n_{r}]\}
. Let
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$},\;\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}\in\mathbf{StIP}
. Then we have

\displaystyle\left\{A\subset\bigcup(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})|\;\mathbf{std}((\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})(A))\geq\mathbf{n}_{1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{k}\right\}

\displaystyle=\biguplus_{0\leq r\leq k}\Big\{A\subset\bigcup(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})|\;\mathbf{std}((\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}))\geq\mathbf{n}_{1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{r},

\displaystyle\qquad\qquad\quad\mathbf{std}((\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}^{\prime}))\geq\mathbf{n}_{r+1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{k}\Big\}.

Proof.

Let

\displaystyle A\subset\bigcup(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})

such that

\displaystyle\mathbf{std}\left((\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})(A)\right)

\displaystyle\geq\mathbf{n}_{1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{k}.

We now show that
\exists!r\in\{0,..k\}
such that

\displaystyle\mathbf{std}\left((\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$})\right)

\displaystyle\geq\mathbf{n}_{1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{r},

\displaystyle\mathbf{std}\left((\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}^{\prime})\right)

\displaystyle\geq\mathbf{n}_{r+1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{k}.

First notice that

\displaystyle\mathbf{std}\left((\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})(A)\right)\geq n_{1}\bullet n_{2}\bullet\cdots\bullet n_{k}

is equivalent to

\displaystyle(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})(A)\geq(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})(A)_{n_{1}\bullet n_{2}\bullet\cdots\bullet n_{k}}

because of
Lemma

3.39
. From
Lemma

3.48
we know
\exists!t\in\{0\}\cup{N}
and therefore
\exists!j_{t}
, where

\displaystyle j_{0}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=0

\displaystyle j_{1},\dots,j_{N}\in\mathbb{N},1\leq j_{1}<\dots<j_{N}=k,1\leq N\leq k.

such that, using also the definition of
\bullet
and the definition of
(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})(A)
, we can write

\displaystyle(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})(A)_{n_{1}\bullet n_{2}\bullet\cdots\bullet n_{k}}=

\displaystyle\{\{\ell_{1},...,\ell_{n_{1}}\},\{\ell_{n_{1}+1},...,\ell_{n_{1}+n_{2}}\},...,\{\ell_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t}-1}n_{i}+1},...,\ell_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t}}n_{i}}\},

\displaystyle\{m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t}}n_{i}+1},...,m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t}+1}n_{i}}\},\{m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t}+1}n_{i}+1},...,m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t}+2}n_{i}}\},

\displaystyle...,\{m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{k-1}n_{i}+1},...,m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{k}n_{i}}\}\}.

where

\displaystyle\ell_{1}\prec\cdots\prec\ell_{n_{1}}<\ell_{n_{1}+1}\prec\cdots\prec\ell_{n_{1}+n_{2}}<\cdots<\ell_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t}-1}n_{i}+1}\prec\cdots\prec\ell_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t}}n_{i}}

\displaystyle<m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t}}n_{i}+1}\prec\cdots\prec m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t}+1}n_{i}}<m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t}+1}n_{i}+1}\prec\cdots\prec m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t}+2}n_{i}}<\cdots

\displaystyle\cdots<m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{k-1}n_{i}+1}\prec\cdots\prec m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{k}n_{i}}.

and

\displaystyle(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})(A)=

\displaystyle\{\{\ell_{1},\dots,\ell_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{1}}n_{i}}\},\{\ell_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{1}}n_{i}+1},\dots,\ell_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{2}}n_{i}}\},\dots,\{\ell_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t-1}}n_{i}+1},\dots,\ell_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t}}n_{i}}\},

\displaystyle\{m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t}}n_{i}+1},\dots,m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t+1}}n_{i}}\},\{m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t+1}}n_{i}+1},\dots,m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t+2}}n_{i}}\},

\displaystyle\dots,\{m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{N-1}}n_{i}+1},\dots,m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{N}}n_{i}}\}\}

where

\displaystyle\ell_{1}\prec\cdots\prec\ell_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{1}}n_{i}}<\ell_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{1}}n_{i}+1}\prec\cdots\prec\ell_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{2}}n_{i}}<\cdots<\ell_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t-1}}n_{i}+1}\prec\cdots\prec\ell_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t}}n_{i}}

\displaystyle<m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t}}n_{i}+1}\prec\cdots\prec m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t+1}}n_{i}}<m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t+1}}n_{i}+1}\prec\cdots\prec m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t+2}}n_{i}}<\cdots

\displaystyle\cdots<m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{N-1}}n_{i}+1}\prec\cdots\prec m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{N}}n_{i}}

where the
\ell
’s are elements of
\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}
and the
m^{\prime}
’s are elements of
\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}^{\prime}
. Recall that
a\prec b\iff b=a+1
.

If we consider

\displaystyle(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$})=

\displaystyle\{\{\ell_{1},\dots,\ell_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{1}}n_{i}}\},\{\ell_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{1}}n_{i}+1},\dots,\ell_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{2}}n_{i}}\},

\displaystyle\dots,\{\ell_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t-1}}n_{i}+1},\dots,\ell_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t}}n_{i}}\}\}

and

\displaystyle(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}^{\prime})=

\displaystyle\{\{m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t}}n_{i}+1},\dots,m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t+1}}n_{i}}\},\{m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t+1}}n_{i}+1},\dots,m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{t+2}}n_{i}}\},

\displaystyle\dots,\{m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{N-1}}n_{i}+1},\dots,m^{\prime}_{\sum_{i=1}^{j_{N}}n_{i}}\}\}.

they satisfy

\displaystyle\mathbf{std}\left((\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$})\right)

\displaystyle\geq\{[n_{1}]\}\bullet\cdots\bullet\{[n_{j_{t}}]\}

\displaystyle\mathbf{std}\left((\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}^{\prime})\right)

\displaystyle\geq\{[n_{j_{t}+1}]\}\bullet\cdots\bullet\{[n_{k}]\}.

∎

Lemma 3.50
.

Let
\mathbf{n}_{1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{k}\in\mathbf{StIP}
, where
k\in\mathbb{N}
and
\forall r\in[k]\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}n_{i}\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 1},\mathbf{n}_{r}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\{[n_{r}]\}
. Let
\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$},\;\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}\in\mathbf{StIP}
. Then we have

\displaystyle\Big|\bigcup_{0\leq r\leq k}\Big\{A\subset\bigcup(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})\Big|\;\mathbf{std}\left((\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$})\right)\geq\mathbf{n}_{1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{r},

\displaystyle\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\mathbf{std}\left((\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}^{\prime})\right)\geq\mathbf{n}_{r+1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{k}\Big\}\Big|

\displaystyle=\Big|\bigcup_{0\leq r\leq k}\Big\{A\subset\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}|\;\mathbf{std}\left(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(A)\right)\geq\mathbf{n}_{1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{r}\Big\}

\displaystyle\qquad\times\Big\{B\subset\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}|\;\mathbf{std}\left(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}(B)\right)\geq\mathbf{n}_{r+1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{k}\Big\}\Big|.

Proof.

We explicitly give a bijection between the two sets.
For some
0\leq r\leq k
let

\displaystyle(A,B)\in\bigcup_{0\leq r\leq k}\{A\subset\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}|\;\mathbf{std}\left(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(A)\right)\geq\mathbf{n}_{1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{r}\}

\displaystyle\times\{B\subset\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}|\;\mathbf{std}\left(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}(B)\right)\geq\mathbf{n}_{r+1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{k}\}

and define the map

\displaystyle(A,B)\mapsto A\cup(B+|\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}|).

Therefore
(B+|\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}|)\subset\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}^{\prime}
and if
B=\emptyset
, set
B+|\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}|\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\emptyset
.
We have

\displaystyle\mathbf{std}\left((\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})((A\cup(B+|\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}|))\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$})\right)=\mathbf{std}\left((\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$})\right)\geq\mathbf{n}_{1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{r}

and

\displaystyle\mathbf{std}\left((\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})((A\cup(B+|\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}|))\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}^{\prime})\right)=\mathbf{std}\left((\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})((B+|\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}|)\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}^{\prime})\right)

\displaystyle=\mathbf{std}\left((\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})(B\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}^{\prime})\right)\geq\mathbf{n}_{r+1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{k}.

Now, let

\displaystyle A\in\bigcup_{0\leq r\leq k}\{A\subset\bigcup(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})|\;\mathbf{std}(\left(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}\right)(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}))\geq\mathbf{n}_{1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{k},

\displaystyle\mathbf{std}\left((\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}^{\prime})\right)\geq\mathbf{n}_{i+1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{k}\}.

Define

\displaystyle A\mapsto(A\cap(\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}),(A\cap(\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}^{\prime}))-|\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}|)

and if
(A\cap(\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}^{\prime}))=\emptyset
, set
(A\cap(\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}^{\prime}))-|\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}|=\emptyset
, which is clearly the inverse of the other map.

∎

Proof of
Theorem

3.46
.

We use
Lemmas

3.48
,
3.49
and
3.50
.

\displaystyle\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}),\mathbf{n}_{1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{k}\Big\rangle

\displaystyle=\#\{A\subset\bigcup(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})|\;\mathbf{std}\left((\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})(A)\right)\geq\mathbf{n}_{1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{k}\}

\displaystyle=\sum_{0\leq i\leq k}\{A\subset\bigcup(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})|\;\mathbf{std}\left((\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$})\right)\geq\mathbf{n}_{1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{i},

\displaystyle\mathbf{std}\left((\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$})(A\cap\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}^{\prime})\right)\geq\mathbf{n}_{i+1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{k}\}

\displaystyle=\sum_{0\leq i\leq k}\#\{A\subset\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}|\;\mathbf{std}\left(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(A)\right)\geq\mathbf{n}_{1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{i}\}

\displaystyle\times\{B\subset\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}|\;\mathbf{std}\left(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}(B)\right)\geq\mathbf{n}_{i+1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{k}\}

\displaystyle=\sum_{0\leq i\leq k}\#\{A|A\subset\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$},\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}(A))\geq\mathbf{n}_{1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{i}\}

\displaystyle\#\{B|B\subset\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$},\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}(B))\geq\mathbf{n}_{i+1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{k}\}

\displaystyle=\sum_{0\leq i\leq k}\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$}),\mathbf{n}_{1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{i}\Big\rangle\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}),\mathbf{n}_{i+1}\bullet\cdots\bullet\mathbf{n}_{k}\Big\rangle

\displaystyle=\Big\langle\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{L}$})\otimes\mathsf{IPC}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{M}$}),\Delta_{\bullet}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$})\Big\rangle.

∎

4
Vincular permutation patterns

In this section, we define a Hopf algebra on pairs which consists of an interval partition of
[n]
and a permutation of length
n
. A pair corresponds to a certain vincular pattern, since the intervals express which values are consecutive in the permutation pattern. It incorporates both the Hopf algebra of

Section

3
and the Hopf algebra appearing in
[
15
]
.
The underlying set is now given by

\displaystyle\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\mathbf{StIP}_{n}\times\mathbf{S}_{n},

general elements of which we denote with
(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},\sigma)
.
We consider the free
\mathbb{Q}
-vector space over it.

Definition 4.1

(
\mathbb{Q}
-vector space over vincular permutations)
.

\displaystyle\mathcal{H}_{\tiny\textbf{vinc}}

\displaystyle\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{StIP}_{n}\times\mathbf{S}_{n}].

(8)

graded by the size of the partitions (or alternatively, the length of permutations).

We now introduce algebraic operations on
\mathcal{H}_{\tiny\textbf{vinc}}
. This can be seen as a “combination” of our Hopf algebra on interval partitions,
\mathcal{H}_{\tiny\textbf{int}}
, and Vargas’ superinfiltration Hopf algebra,
\mathcal{H}_{\tiny\textbf{per}}
.

4.1
Algebraic operations

We recall the operations of the superinfiltration Hopf algebra introduced in
[
15
]
.

Definition 4.2

(Superinfiltration product,
[
15
]
)
.

Let
\sigma,\tau\in\mathbf{S}
.

\displaystyle\sigma\ \raisebox{2.15277pt}{\rotatebox[origin]{90.0}{$\Rightarrow$}}\ \tau

\displaystyle\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\sum_{\gamma\in\mathbf{S}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}A\cup B=[|\gamma|]\\
\mathbf{st}(\gamma\,\raisebox{-3.98611pt}{$|_{A}$})=\sigma,\mathbf{st}(\gamma\,\raisebox{-3.98611pt}{$|_{B}$})=\tau\end{subarray}}\gamma.

Definition 4.3

(
[
15
]
)
.

Let
\sigma\in\mathbf{S}
.

\displaystyle\Delta_{\square}(\sigma)

\displaystyle\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\sum_{\alpha\square\beta}\alpha\otimes\beta,

where for
\alpha\in\mathbf{S}_{m}
and
\beta\in\mathbf{S}_{n}
we have
\alpha\square\beta\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\alpha_{1}\dots\alpha_{m}(\beta_{1}+m)\dots(\beta_{n}+m)
.

Then,
(\mathcal{H}_{\tiny\textbf{per}},\raisebox{2.15277pt}{\rotatebox[origin]{90.0}{$\Rightarrow$}},\Delta_{\,\square})
, is a connected filtered Hopf algebra

[
15
, Corollary 4.8]
.

Remark 4.4

(Malvenuto-Reutenauer Hopf algebra on permutations)
.

In
[
15
]
, the supershuffle coproduct

\displaystyle\Delta_{\,\scriptsize\underline{\shuffle}\;}(\sigma)

\displaystyle\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}A,B\subset[|\sigma|]\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}\\
A\uplus B=[|\sigma|]\end{subarray}}\mathbf{st}\left(\sigma\,\raisebox{-5.11108pt}{$|_{A}$}\right)\otimes\mathbf{st}\left(\sigma\,\raisebox{-5.11108pt}{$|_{B}$}\right).

also appears. Vargas has showed that
(\mathcal{H}_{\tiny\textbf{per}},\underline{\shuffle},\Delta_{\square})
is a Hopf algebra. The supershuffle,
\underline{\shuffle}
, incorporates the algebraic operations of the Malvenuto-Reutenauer Hopf Algebra
on permutations,
(\mathcal{H}_{\tiny\textbf{per}},*^{\prime},\Delta_{*})
,
[
10
]
. If
\sigma\in\mathbf{S}_{m},\tau\in\mathbf{S}_{n}

\displaystyle\sigma*^{\prime}\tau

\displaystyle\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\sigma\,\shuffle\,\tau_{m},

\displaystyle\Delta_{*}(\sigma)

\displaystyle\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\sum_{i=0}^{n}\mathbf{st}(\sigma_{1}\cdots\sigma_{i})\otimes\mathbf{st}(\sigma_{i+1}\cdots\sigma_{n}).

where
\shuffle
is the usual shuffle product on words and
\tau_{m}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=(\tau_{1}+m)\cdots(\tau_{n}+m)
. We present a few computations as examples.

\displaystyle\Delta_{*}(1243)

\displaystyle=\mathsf{e}\otimes 1243+1\otimes 132+12\otimes 21+123\otimes 1+1243\otimes\mathsf{e},

\displaystyle 12\,\underline{\shuffle}\,21

\displaystyle=1243+1324+{\color[rgb]{1,0,0}2}\;1342+{\color[rgb]{1,0,0}2}\;1423+{\color[rgb]{1,0,0}3}\;1432+2134+{\color[rgb]{1,0,0}2}\;2314

\displaystyle+{\color[rgb]{1,0,0}3}\;2341+2413+{\color[rgb]{1,0,0}2}\;2431+{\color[rgb]{1,0,0}2}\;3124

\displaystyle+3142+{\color[rgb]{1,0,0}3}\;3214+{\color[rgb]{1,0,0}2}\;3241+3421

\displaystyle+{\color[rgb]{1,0,0}3}\;4123+{\color[rgb]{1,0,0}2}\;4132+{\color[rgb]{1,0,0}2}\;4213+4231+4312,

\displaystyle 12*21

\displaystyle=1243+1342+1432+2341+2431+3421,

\displaystyle 12*^{\prime}21

\displaystyle=1243+1423+4123+1432+4312+4132.

4.1.1
Products, coproducts

We now endow
\mathcal{H}_{\tiny\textbf{vinc}}
with a Hopf algebra structure.

The product combines the products
\bullet
(
Definition

3.19
) and
\square
(
Definition

4.3
).

Definition 4.5
.

We define on basis elements,
(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},\sigma),(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$},\tau)\in\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\mathbf{StIP}_{n}\times\mathbf{S}_{n}

\displaystyle(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},\sigma)\resizebox{}{39322}{$\blacksquare$}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$},\tau)\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\bullet\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$},\sigma\square\tau).

and then extend linearly.

Proposition 4.6

(Associativity)
.

The product

\blacksquare

is associative.

Proof.

Since
\bullet
and
\square
are associative products, the result follows.
∎

Remark 4.8
.

Its dual coproduct
is

\displaystyle\Delta_{\resizebox{}{26214}{$\blacksquare$}}((\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},\sigma))\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\sum_{\mathfrak{a}\bullet\mathfrak{b}=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\alpha\square\beta=\sigma\\
\alpha\in\mathbf{S}_{|\bigcup\mathfrak{a}|},\,\beta\in\mathbf{S}_{|\bigcup\mathfrak{b}|}\end{subarray}}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},\sigma)\otimes(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$},\tau)

Definition 4.9
.

On basis elements,
\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\mathbf{StIP}_{n}\times\mathbf{S}_{n}
, we define

\displaystyle\Delta_{{\text{\color[rgb]{0.74,1,0.24}♥}}}\left((\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},\sigma)\right)

\displaystyle\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\sum_{A\cup A^{\prime}=\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}}\;\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathcal{I}\in\mathbf{IP}(A),\;\mathcal{I}^{\prime}\in\mathbf{IP}(A^{\prime})\\
\\
\mathcal{I}\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\mathcal{I}^{\prime}=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$}\end{subarray}}(\mathbf{std}\left(\mathcal{I}\right),\mathbf{st}(\sigma\,\raisebox{-5.0pt}{$|_{A}$}))\otimes(\mathbf{std}\left(\mathcal{I}^{\prime}\right),\mathbf{st}(\sigma\,\raisebox{-5.0pt}{$|_{A^{\prime}}$})).

and extend linearly. Its dual product is defined as

\displaystyle(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},\sigma){\text{\color[rgb]{0.74,1,0.24}♥}}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$},\tau)

\displaystyle\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$},\gamma)\in\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\mathbf{StIP}_{n}\times\mathbf{S}_{n}\\
\\
A\cup A^{\prime}=\bigcup\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\end{subarray}}\;\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathcal{I}\in\mathbf{IP}(A),\;\mathcal{I}^{\prime}\in\mathbf{IP}(A^{\prime})\\
\\
\mathbf{std}\left(\mathcal{I}\right)=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{s}$},\;\mathbf{std}\left(\mathcal{I}^{\prime}\right)=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{t}$}\\
\\
\mathcal{I}\cdot_{\textbf{{glue}}}\mathcal{I}^{\prime}=\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$}\end{subarray}}\sum_{\mathbf{st}(\gamma\,\raisebox{-3.98611pt}{$|_{A}$})=\sigma,\mathbf{st}(\gamma\,\raisebox{-3.98611pt}{$|_{A^{\prime}}$})=\tau}(\resizebox{}{655360}{$\mathfrak{g}$},\gamma).
